Plant the Moon Final Report: Who Let the Plants Out? Team 13284
How a Self-Sustaining Environment with Different Amounts of Water Affects
Marigolds and Green Beans Growth in 50% Lunar Regolith and 50% Potting Soil
with Additives
Background:
We chose to conduct an experiment on plants with domes on the top. We wanted to
reduce the amount of water needed to sustain plants because there is not a lot of water
on the Moon.

Experiment Design:
This experiment was conducted in Manchester Essex Middle School, room A117. We
started after February break ended and we ended before April break. How we did this
experiment was that we took measurements every day our class met. We were
measuring the height of the Marigolds and Green Beans and how many leaves or petals
they had. We watered them on different days and amounts based on the pot and we
measured the pH every other week. Please see the grow pot setup below.

Question or Hypotheses:
How does a self-sustaining environment with different amounts of water affect marigold
and green bean growth in 50% lunar regolith and 50% potting soil with additives?
Independent Variables or Parameters:
There were lots of things changing between our pots. The first thing that changed
between our pots was the amount of water the plants got. For example each pot for
marigolds and green beans had a different amount of water they got each week. The
first pot for both plants had 1 inch on Tuesday and on Thursday. The second pot got 2
inches of water on Tuesday, the third pot got 1 inch on Tuesday, and the fourth pot got
.5 inches of water a week.

The second thing we changed is the type of seed. Five pots had marigolds and five pots
had green beans.We chose marigolds because they look good, grow well, and can be
eaten. They have a PH of 6.2-6.5. It takes 8 weeks for the flower to blossom, 4 to 14
days to grow, and needs full sun. We chose green beans because they don’t take that
long to grow and they are good to eat. They have a 6.5-6.7 PH. We put domes on the
plants, to make a self - sustainable environment.
Measurements & Procedures:
In our procedure, we were required to measure most of our data; we measured the pH
of the regolith, the moisture content of the soil, and the plant growth. We used a ruler for
the growth measurement, we used a pH scale for measuring the pH, and as for testing
the moisture of the soil, we usually looked at it and felt the regolith to see if it was dry or
wet. Our procedure for measuring was recording the data daily for the first fifteen
minutes of class in Middle School Academy. We started recording after February break
on March 3rd, we replanted on March 21st and stopped recording after our plants died for
the second time on March 31st.

Controls:
For Marigolds we kept regolith - 50% and Potting Soil 50%, and we also kept 1 tsp of
fertilizer the same. Lastly, Marigolds need 6-8 hours of sunlight each day, and We used
1” of compost and 10-10-10 fertilizer.
For Green Beans we kept regolith - 50% and potting soil - 50%. For fertilizer, we kept it
at 0.5 tsp. Then they were placed under light for 6 hours a day. We used 1” of compost
and 10-10-10 fertilizer.
Our controls had no domes, whereas other plants had domes.

Dependent Variable:
We measured the height of both plants, we also measured the number of leaves on
both of the plants, the PH of the plants, and if the plants needed to be watered.
Results:
On March 3 we planted 5 germinated marigolds and 5 germinated green beans into
separate plastic pots. We planted the marigolds with lunar soil, potting soil, compost,
and 10-10-10 fertilizer. We planted the green beans with lunar soil, potting soil,
compost, and 10-10-10 fertilizer and domes on 8 pots. There was neither height nor
leaves for 18 days and that's when we realized the marigolds and green beans were not
going to grow at all, so we decided to replant. On March 21 we replanted 5 different
germinated bok choi and 5 germinated romaine plants and took them off the grow lights.
Placing them on the window ledge would give the plants natural light. We expected that
after a few days the bok choi and romaine plants would begin to sprout but we were
incorrect. Nothing sprouted. With four days left with this experiment, we decided to not
replant. Please see the data chart below.

Analysis and Conclusions:
Our question was how does a self-sustaining environment with different amounts of
water affect marigolds and green beans growth in 50% lunar regolith and 50% potting
soil with additives. Our experiment proved that marigolds and green beans encountered
too much stress given small amounts of water. The green beans never even
germinated, whilst the marigolds did start to grow roots in the bag they were
germinating in. However, they shortly died after planting due to high amounts of stress
in the acidic soil. We then planted additional plants, (5 romaine plants, and 5 bok choy
plants) but they then died. We never saw any growth above the soil, showing that
reduced amounts of water negatively impacted the plant growth.
